jobs.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

We're living through a fundamental shift in how people discover, evaluate, and purchase products. The next generation doesn't respond to traditional marketing -- they build relationships with brands through authentic social interactions, seek recommendations from communities they trust, and expect personalized experiences that feel human, not corporate.

At Nectar, we're building the AI-native social operating system that enables this new era of commerce. We believe every social interaction should deepen the relationship between brands and their communities while creating genuine value for both sides.

Founded by ex-Meta product and engineering leaders, we've raised over $30M in total capital from investors including GV and True Ventures. We work with brands like Oura Health, Caraway, e.l.f. Cosmetics, Kosas, OLIPOP, and many more. We're building the future of social commerce -- where community, conversation, and commerce converge.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategy for Nectar's platform. Reporting directly to the VP, GTM, you'll play a critical role in defining how we communicate our value to customers and how we win in the market.

This is a high-impact role where you'll help shape the product marketing function as we scale. You'll work closely with sales, product, and leadership to craft compelling narratives, launch new capabilities, and strengthen our competitive positioning.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Develop and refine Nectar's positioning and messaging across different customer segments, including enterprise, mid-market, and emerging brands

  • Build and maintain competitive intelligence programs, creating battle cards and differentiation narratives for the sales team

  • Own product launches end-to-end, from positioning and naming to internal enablement and launch campaigns

  • Create sales enablement materials such as pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, and ROI calculators

  • Partner closely with the sales team to understand buyer personas, refine our ideal customer profile, and improve win rates

  • Synthesize customer feedback, competitive trends, and market insights to inform product strategy and roadmap decisions

  • Support company storytelling and fundraising efforts with compelling market narratives and positioning

What We're Looking For

  • 4–7 years of product marketing experience, ideally in B2B SaaS

  • Experience owning positioning and messaging for a product or product line

  • Strong experience partnering with sales teams to build sales enablement programs

  • Ability to conduct competitive analysis and translate insights into actionable positioning and strategy

  • Excellent writing, communication, and storytelling abilities

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous environments and building new functions in a fast-moving startup

  • Strong collaboration skills across product, sales, and leadership teams

Bonus Points

  • Experience in martech, social media platforms, or commerce-related software

  • Experience working at a company through a Series A or Series B growth phase

  • Experience launching AI-powered products or technical platforms

  • Background working closely with enterprise sales teams

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and early equity

  • Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

  • Hybrid work schedule (4 days in office) with 3 flex remote days per quarter (available after 3 months)

  • Comprehensive stipends: $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office, $50/month mobile stipend, $50/month internet stipend for remote employees, and commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking permit reimbursement)

  • Free lunch in the office

The Role

We're looking for a software engineer to help architect and scale the core systems that power Nectar's platform. You'll work on the infrastructure that ingests, processes, and analyzes large volumes of social data while enabling AI agents to operate on that data in real time.

This role combines deep technical execution with architectural leadership. You'll help define how our systems evolve as we scale customers, data volume, and product capabilities.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Architect and scale the core systems that ingest and process large volumes of social data from platforms like Instagram, TikTok, X, Reddit, and LinkedIn

  • Design data pipelines that power AI agents and real-time analytics used by our customers

  • Lead major technical decisions across the platform, writing design docs and establishing scalable architecture patterns

  • Improve reliability, performance, and cost efficiency across our data and AI infrastructure as the platform scales

  • Mentor engineers and review system designs and code to help raise the engineering bar across the team

  • Work closely with product and engineering leadership to solve complex technical problems and deliver impactful systems

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience building and operating production software systems

  • Strong experience designing and scaling distributed systems, data infrastructure, or complex production platforms

  • Proven ability to architect systems and drive major technical decisions

  • Experience mentoring engineers and influencing engineering direction

  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving startup environments with high ownership and autonomy

  • Strong product intuition and ability to collaborate closely with product and design teams

  • Interest in AI-native engineering workflows and how AI is transforming software development

Bonus Points

  • Startup experience building early-stage or rapidly scaling products

  • Experience working with large-scale data pipelines or real-time analytics systems

  • Familiarity with modern infrastructure and developer tooling such as AWS, Pulumi, Postgres, ClickHouse, or similar technologies

  • Experience integrating AI or machine learning systems into production platforms

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and early equity

  • Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

  • ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

  • Hybrid schedule: 4 days in office, plus 3 remote flex days per quarter (after your first 3 months)

  • Comprehensive stipends: $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office, $50/month mobile stipend, and commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking reimbursement)

  • Free lunch in the office

  • Clear career growth opportunities as the company scales

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager, AI to lead the development of AI-powered capabilities across Nectar's platform. You'll work closely with engineering and leadership to build AI-native workflows that deliver measurable impact for customers while shaping how AI is embedded throughout our product experience.

  • Partner closely with engineering teams to build and refine generative prompting systems, AI workflows, and model-powered features

  • Define and track key performance metrics for AI-driven features such as automation impact, engagement outcomes, and accuracy

  • Identify high-impact opportunities to apply AI across social engagement, personalization, and operational workflows

  • Write product specifications, test features, and iterate quickly in a fast-moving startup environment

  • Stay informed on industry developments across AI, generative technologies, and social commerce

  • Strong analytical skills with experience defining metrics and using data to guide product decisions

  • Experience working with or strong interest in AI/ML technologies, particularly generative AI or prompting workflows

  • Background in social commerce, creator economy tools, or enterprise SaaS products

  • Experience building products for consumer brands or marketing teams

  • MBA or a track record of exceptional academic or professional achievement

  • Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

  • ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

  • Free lunch in the office

  • Clear career growth opportunities as the company scales

The Role

We're looking for a Founding Mobile Engineer to own and define the mobile experience at Nectar. You'll architect and build the mobile platform from the ground up, making foundational technical decisions that shape how we deliver AI-powered social commerce to brand teams.

This is a highly autonomous role with direct influence over product direction and engineering standards. You'll work closely with product, design, and leadership to ship features that bring Nectar's AI capabilities directly into the hands of customers.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the mobile platform end-to-end, architecting, building, and shipping our React Native application across iOS and Android

  • Build AI-powered mobile experiences that surface insights, power real-time agent interactions, and bring Nectar's AI capabilities to mobile

  • Establish mobile architecture patterns, shared components, testing strategies, CI/CD pipelines, and performance standards

  • Integrate with social platform APIs such as TikTok, Meta, and Instagram, as well as e-commerce systems like Shopify

  • Collaborate closely with product, design, and founders to shape both the product experience and technical implementation

  • Set a high bar for reliability and performance through monitoring, error tracking, and optimization

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience with deep expertise in React Native

  • Proven track record of shipping high-quality production mobile applications

  • Strong understanding of mobile architecture, navigation patterns, state management, and platform-specific considerations

  • Experience integrating with external APIs and building real-time, data-intensive features

  • Comfortable working across the stack when needed in a fast-moving startup environment

  • High ownership mindset with a bias toward action and comfort operating in ambiguity

  • Strong product intuition and interest in shaping what gets built, not just how it gets built

Bonus Points

  • Experience with native iOS or Android development or bridging native modules

  • Background in social media platforms, e-commerce systems, or commerce infrastructure

  • Experience working with LLMs, AI agents, or machine learning-powered features in production

  • Previous founding or early-stage startup experience

  • Open-source contributions or notable side projects

    • Free lunch in the office

  • ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

The Role

You'll be our first dedicated Revenue Strategy and Operations hire, reporting to our Head of Operations. Today, RevOps at Nectar lives inside a broader operations function that also covers finance, legal, and people. You'll take ownership of the revenue side of that house — the sales stack, forecasting, deal desk, commissions, and the connective tissue between sales, marketing, CS, and finance — and build it into a function.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll inherit working systems (Salesforce, a live forecasting model, a freshly launched FY27 commission framework, integrated tooling across Pylon, Granola, Slack, and our finance stack) and you'll be expected to run them day one, then make them better. As we scale, you'll have a clear path to leading Revenue Operations as a team.

What You'll Own

Salesforce & GTM Systems

  • Serve as our Salesforce administrator: objects, flows, validation rules, reporting, user management, and data hygiene across the full pipeline

  • Own the GTM tech stack end to end — evaluate, implement, integrate, and retire tools (current stack includes Salesforce, Pylon, Granola, Slack, and integrations into our billing/ERP systems)

  • Build and maintain integrations between sales systems and finance systems (e.g., Salesforce ↔ Rillet), ensuring clean quote-to-cash data flow

Forecasting & Pipeline

  • Own the weekly forecasting cadence: pipeline reviews, forecast rollups, and board-level reporting on bookings, pipeline coverage, and conversion

  • Maintain and evolve our forecast model against a non-standard fiscal calendar (FY runs Feb–Jan)

  • Instrument the funnel from marketing through closed-won so leadership can see conversion, velocity, and drop-off by stage and segment

Deal Desk & Pricing Operations

  • Run deal desk for enterprise and mid-market deals: order forms, pricing approvals, discount governance, and non-standard deal structures (pilots, multi-brand rollouts, ramp deals)

  • Partner with Legal on contract workflows — you won't negotiate MSAs, but you'll own the operational machinery that gets order forms drafted, approved, signed, and booked correctly

  • Maintain pricing infrastructure: rate cards, pricing calculators, and approval guardrails

Compensation & Quota Administration

  • Administer commission plans for AEs and AI Strategists: monthly/quarterly calculations, accruals with Finance, disputes, and plan documentation

  • Support annual quota setting, territory design, and comp plan iteration with sales leadership

Marketing Ops (initially)

  • Own lead routing, attribution basics, and campaign-to-pipeline reporting until we make a dedicated marketing ops hire

Our engineering organization includes multiple core teams with a strong product-facing focus, as well as a Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team that moves fast across the full stack on high-priority initiatives. Your team will build products that ingest large volumes of social data, run AI agents on that data in real time, and deliver insights to customers through analytics and automation.

You will be deeply involved in what gets built and how it gets built. You’ll sit in customer calls, develop strong opinions about product strategy, and partner with Product and Design as a technical peer. At the same time, you’ll drive systemic code quality, establish system architecture, mentor senior technical talent, and guide technical direction as we scale from ~50 people into our next phase of growth.



WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Technical Architecture & Strategy: Define the technical roadmap, system design, and architectural standards for your product domain to ensure high performance, scalability, and maintainability.

 - Hands-On Execution & Delivery: Lead by example. Write production code, conduct thorough code reviews, solve complex technical bottlenecks, and own critical path architecture for key initiatives.

 - Product & Design Partnership: Partner closely with Product and Design to evaluate feasibility, scope features, and refine requirements. Bring a strong technical perspective to user problems and product direction.

 - Technical Mentorship & Quality: Coach and mentor engineers across the team. Raise the technical bar through pair programming, architecture reviews, and fostering best practices in software craftsmanship.

 - Customer Empathy: Sit in customer calls regularly to build direct technical intuition for how social and brand teams use our products and where system performance or UX falls short.

 - Engineering Standards & Process: Drive technical excellence across the lifecycle—refining RFC processes, testing strategies, CI/CD pipelines, system monitoring, and post-mortem resolutions.

 - Hiring & Technical Assessment: Help scale the engineering team by conducting technical interviews, reviewing system design assessments, and evaluating top-tier engineering talent.

 - People Management: Own formal management responsibilities for a team of 2-5  — regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career growth planning.
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience Level: 8+ years of total software engineering experience, with 2+ years formally managing direct reports (people management, not just technical leadership) on a high-performing engineering team.

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Proven experience working alongside Product Managers and Product Designers, particularly in fast-paced startup environments where roles cross over seamlessly.

 - Startup Agility: A strong bias toward action and comfort operating in high-growth, ambiguous environments with changing priorities.

 - Communication: Exceptional, direct written and verbal communication skills with a track record of translating complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders.

 - AI Literacy: Active hands-on experience or deep technical interest in incorporating LLMs, AI agents, and modern AI workflows into software architecture.

 - Startup Experience: Prior experience working at an early or growth-stage startup, comfortable with the ambiguity and pace that comes with it.

 - AI-Powered Systems: Hands-on experience architecting, deploying, or operating AI-powered or agentic software platforms at scale.

 - Tech Stack Familiarity: Hands-on experience with React, TypeScript, AWS, Pulumi, Postgres, ClickHouse, or Turbopuffer.

 - Mobile Experience: Prior technical leadership on teams shipping mobile products, ideally using React Native.

 - Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

 - ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

 - Hybrid schedule: 4 days in office, plus 3 remote flex days per quarter (after your first 3 months)

 - Comprehensive stipends: $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office, $50/month mobile stipend, and commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking reimbursement)

  • Own end-to-end planning and execution for Nectar's West Coast event calendar across SF and LA: customer dinners, executive roundtables, happy hours, creator meetups, and conference sponsorships and booths.

  • Run account-based event programs with sales: executive dinners and roundtables built around target accounts, with a follow-up plan for every attendee.

  • Build a recurring event series in both cities so Nectar has a consistent, recognizable presence in each market.

  • Manage budgets, vendors, venues, and logistics in both cities, and build repeatable processes so events scale smoothly as the company grows.

  • Partner with sales and customer success on event strategies that generate pipeline and deepen relationships with existing customers.

  • Track and report on event ROI (attendance, sourced and influenced pipeline, and customer sentiment), and use that data to sharpen the calendar over time.

  • Represent Nectar at West Coast industry conferences and manage on-site logistics, staffing, and sponsor deliverables.

Community

  • Support the launch and growth of Nectar's customer and industry community program (e.g., a Slack community, ambassador program, or customer council).

  • Help run the content and engagement cadence that keeps the community active: AMAs, office hours, member spotlights, and peer-to-peer discussion.

  • Use in-person events to feed the community, turning SF and LA attendees into active members.

  • Build authentic relationships with key West Coast customers, creators, and industry voices.

  • Identify and cultivate community advocates who can support case studies, referrals, and word-of-mouth growth.

  • Feed community insights and feedback back to the product, marketing, and customer success teams.

What You'll Bring

  • 5-8 years of experience in B2B event marketing, community management, or a hybrid of both, with most of it at B2B SaaS companies.

  • A track record of running B2B field and executive events end-to-end, from concept through post-event reporting, that sourced and accelerated pipeline alongside sales.

  • Fluency in B2B event measurement: campaign attribution in HubSpot or Salesforce, sourced versus influenced pipeline, and post-event follow-up with target accounts.

  • Experience supporting or growing an online or in-person community.

  • Based in or near Palo Alto, with working knowledge of the Bay Area and LA event scenes: the venues, the vendors, and the people worth knowing.

  • Comfort operating with high autonomy in an early-stage environment where processes don't exist yet. You're excited to build them.

  • Strong project management skills and the ability to juggle multiple events across two markets without dropping details.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with a real interest in connecting with people.

  • Willingness to travel regularly to San Francisco, Los Angeles, and industry conferences (estimated 20-30%).

Nice to Have

  • Experience in the social media, marketing technology, or creator economy space.

  • Experience marketing to brand, social, or marketing leaders as the buyer.

  • An existing network in Bay Area tech and in LA's consumer brand or creator communities.

  • Familiarity with community platforms (Slack, Discord, Circle) and event tools (Luma, Bizzabo, HubSpot).

  • Prior experience as an early hire at a startup, building a function from zero to one.

  • Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

  • ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

  • Free lunch in the office

  • $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office

  • Fully paid for commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking reimbursement)

We're hiring our first GTM Engineer to build the internal tools our sales and marketing teams run on, and to help design an outbound motion from the ground up.

Spray-and-pray is dead. "Personalized" outbound is close behind, as every inbox is full of AI-written emails that reference some signal. You’ll be helping develop what comes next: outreach built on warm intros, real signals, and data only we have, that a thoughtful person is actually glad to receive. You'll help define it, build the systems behind it, and prove with numbers what works. You will get comfortable experimenting and building the end-to-end systems to enable those experiments.

  • Internal tools. When someone in sales, marketing, or even the C-Suite says "we have an idea," you're the one who says "let's build it," and has a working version in their hands within days.   • Experience with Clay, n8n, Gong, and Salesforce

  • Background in martech, social data, or selling to consumer brands

  • Prior founding-team or first-GTM-engineer experience

  • Experience at a company with a sales team of 50-100 — you've seen what enablement looks like at scale

  • Have built or meaningfully rebuilt an enablement program yourself, not just maintained inherited content

  • Experience designing onboarding, certification, or pitch-practice programs for AEs

  • Strong communication and presentation skills; comfortable coaching reps and giving direct feedback

  • Process-oriented and organized, with the ability to build systems from zero

Bonus Qualifications

  • Started your career in B2B sales (AE or SDR) or product marketing before moving into enablement

  • Background in martech, social media, or AI/automation platforms

  • Familiarity with selling to consumer brands (beauty, CPG, e-commerce, retail)

  • Experience standing up enablement tools (e.g., Highspot, Seismic, Gong, Lessonly)

  • Fluency with AI-native tools for building content and training

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and early equity

  • Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

  • ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

  • $50/month mobile stipend for all employees, and $50/month internet stipend for remote employees

For our Palo Alto Office:

  • Hybrid schedule: 4 days in office, plus 3 remote flex days per quarter (after your first 3 months)

  • Free lunch in the office

  • $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office

  • Fully paid for commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking reimbursement)

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll inherit working systems (Salesforce, a live forecasting model, a freshly launched FY27 commission framework, integrated tooling across Pylon, Granola, Slack, and our finance stack) and you'll be expected to run them day one, then make them better. As we scale, you'll have a clear path to leading Revenue Operations as a team.

 

What You'll Own

Salesforce & GTM Systems

  • Serve as our Salesforce administrator: objects, flows, validation rules, reporting, user management, and data hygiene across the full pipeline

  • Own the GTM tech stack end to end — evaluate, implement, integrate, and retire tools (current stack includes Salesforce, Pylon, Granola, Slack, and integrations into our billing/ERP systems)

  • Build and maintain integrations between sales systems and finance systems (e.g., Salesforce ↔ Rillet), ensuring clean quote-to-cash data flow

Forecasting & Pipeline

  • Own the weekly forecasting cadence: pipeline reviews, forecast rollups, and board-level reporting on bookings, pipeline coverage, and conversion

  • Maintain and evolve our forecast model against a non-standard fiscal calendar (FY runs Feb–Jan)

  • Instrument the funnel from marketing through closed-won so leadership can see conversion, velocity, and drop-off by stage and segment

Deal Desk & Pricing Operations

  • Run deal desk for enterprise and mid-market deals: order forms, pricing approvals, discount governance, and non-standard deal structures (pilots, multi-brand rollouts, ramp deals)

  • Partner with Legal on contract workflows — you won't negotiate MSAs, but you'll own the operational machinery that gets order forms drafted, approved, signed, and booked correctly

  • Maintain pricing infrastructure: rate cards, pricing calculators, and approval guardrails

Compensation & Quota Administration

  • Administer commission plans for AEs and AI Strategists: monthly/quarterly calculations, accruals with Finance, disputes, and plan documentation

  • Support annual quota setting, territory design, and comp plan iteration with sales leadership

Marketing Ops (initially)

  • Own lead routing, attribution basics, and campaign-to-pipeline reporting until we make a dedicated marketing ops hire

  • Keep marketing and sales data connected so pipeline sources are trustworthy

 

Your First 90 Days

  • Take over the weekly forecast cadence immediately and Salesforce administration by end of quarter, with zero disruption to the sales team

  • Run a full quarter of commission calculations under the new FY27 plan and fix what breaks

  • Ship one meaningful automation that removes manual work from quote-to-cash

  • Deliver a RevOps roadmap for the next 12 months: what we build, buy, and kill

 

Who You Are

  • 2–6 years of experience in one of two profiles: (a) hands-on revenue or sales operations at a B2B SaaS company — ideally one that scaled through Series A/B while you were there, or (b) 2–3 years in management consulting, banking, or a similarly rigorous analytical environment, with clear evidence you can go deep on systems, not just analysis

  • Systems aptitude, fast. You'll become our Salesforce administrator within your first quarter. Prior admin experience is a strong plus; what's non-negotiable is demonstrated ability to master technical tools quickly and independently — you've built complex models, automated workflows, written SQL, or taught yourself a platform under deadline pressure

  • You've touched money. Commission administration, deal desk, billing handoffs, or quote-to-cash — you understand that RevOps errors show up in people's paychecks and the company's revenue recognition, and you're precise accordingly

  • Spreadsheet-native and increasingly AI-native. Advanced Excel/Sheets is table stakes; SQL and comfort using AI tools to automate your own work are strong pluses

  • Structured thinker, scrappy executor. You can build a framework and a slide, but you'd rather ship the fix. If you're coming from consulting or banking, you're running toward the operating work, not away from client hours

  • High ownership, low ego. At 60 people there's no one to delegate to. You'll do the unglamorous work (data cleanup, order form QA) alongside the strategic work, and you'll see both as the job

Nice to Have

  • Experience with usage-based or hybrid pricing models

  • Experience administering commission tooling (CaptivateIQ, Spiff, QuotaPath) or building comp calcs from scratch

  • Exposure to CPQ implementation or evaluation

  • Familiarity with modern finance stacks (Rillet, NetSuite, or similar) and procurement portals (Coupa, Ariba)

  • Prior "first ops hire" or founding-team experience

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and early equity

  • Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

  • ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

  • Hybrid schedule: 4 days in office, plus 3 remote flex days per quarter (after your first 3 months)

  • Comprehensive stipends: $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office, $50/month mobile stipend, and commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking reimbursement)

  • Free lunch in the office

  • Clear career growth opportunities as the company scales

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

We're living through a fundamental shift in how people discover, evaluate, and purchase products. The next generation doesn't respond to traditional marketing -- they build relationships with brands through authentic social interactions, seek recommendations from communities they trust, and expect personalized experiences that feel human, not corporate.

At Nectar, we're building the AI-native social operating system that enables this new era of commerce. We believe every social interaction should deepen the relationship between brands and their communities while creating genuine value for both sides.

Founded by ex-Meta product and engineering leaders, we've raised over $30M in total capital from investors including GV and True Ventures. We work with brands like Oura Health, Caraway, e.l.f. Cosmetics, Kosas, OLIPOP, and many more. We're building the future of social commerce -- where community, conversation, and commerce converge.

The Role

We're hiring a Contract Technical Recruiter to help us scale our engineering, data, and product teams. Our engineering organization is around 50 people and growing, and we're hiring across software engineering, engineering leadership, product, and data science. You'll own searches end to end, from intake to signed offer, and help us hire people who raise the bar.

You'll partner directly with our founders, engineering leaders, and hiring managers, and you'll be the first impression many candidates have of Nectar. This role is based in our Palo Alto office.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for technical roles, including software engineers, tech leads, engineering managers, product managers, and data scientists

  • Run intake meetings with hiring managers to define the role, the profile, the interview plan, and what a great hire looks like

  • Source passive candidates through LinkedIn, Juicebox, GitHub, referrals, sourcing tools, and your own network, and write outreach that gets replies

  • Screen candidates for technical fit, motivation, and alignment with how we work, and present a clear, honest pitch for Nectar

  • Coordinate interview loops and keep candidates and interviewers moving quickly, with feedback collected and debriefs held on time

  • Manage offers and closing conversations alongside hiring managers and founders, including compensation and equity discussions

  • Keep our ATS (Ashby) accurate and up to date, and report on pipeline health, conversion rates, and time to hire

  • Give candidates a fast, transparent, and personal experience at every stage, whether or not they get an offer

  • Suggest improvements to our interview process, job descriptions, and sourcing strategy as we scale

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of technical recruiting experience, ideally including time at a high-growth startup, venture-backed company.

  • A track record of closing software engineers and engineering leaders in a competitive market such as the Bay Area

  • Strong sourcing skills; you can find and engage passive candidates rather than waiting on inbound

  • Enough technical fluency to talk credibly with engineers about stacks, systems, and the work they'd do here

  • Experience managing several open searches at once while keeping hiring managers and candidates informed

  • Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication, and comfort advising hiring managers when a search needs to change course

  • Hands-on experience with a modern ATS (Ashby preferred) and sourcing tools, and comfort using AI tools such as Claude to work faster

  • Able to work from our Palo Alto office 4 days a week
